rows.criterion: Sole Bidder must be registered under Indian Companies Act, 1956 / 2013 or partnership firms registered or under Limited Liability Partnerships (registered under LLP Act, 2008).
rows.note: Meridian Infratech Limited is incorporated on 14 March 2016 under the Companies Act 2013 (CIN U72900MH2016PLC287341).

rows.criterion: Sole Bidder must be in the business of IT/ITeS and should have successfully undertaken software development or IT project implementation anywhere in India at least in the 7 (seven) years prior to date of bid submission.
rows.note: The profile lists multiple India IT/ITeS implementations from 2021–2024 (e.g., state portal, land records, PSU data-centre, municipal platform).

rows.criterion: Average annual turnover of Sole Bidder during the immediate three preceding financial years ending on 31st March 2025 which have been audited should be at least INR 250 Cr; only standalone turnover of the bidding entity will be considered (no parent/subsidiary/associate turnover).
rows.note: Standalone average annual turnover is INR 268.4 Cr for FY 2022-23 to FY 2024-25; audited statements are available.

rows.criterion: The Net Worth of Sole Bidder should be Positive for each of the last three financial years ending on 31st March 2025.
rows.note: Net worth is stated as positive in each of the last three financial years.

rows.criterion: Sole Bidder must have been awarded IT Turnkey-Projects for Central Govt. / State Govt. / Urban Local Bodies / Government Corporations/ Government companies/ PSUs sector in India during the 7 years prior to the date of submission of bids: One (01) project, amount > INR 50 Cr.; OR Two (02) projects, amount for each is > INR 30 Cr.; OR Three (03) projects, amount for each is > INR 20 Cr.; (cumulative value for additions/extensions/CRs for the same project will be considered).
rows.note: They have three eligible government/PSU projects each > INR 20 Cr (34.6 Cr; 28.2 Cr; 21.4 Cr) within the last 7 years.

rows.criterion: Sole Bidder should have experience of Design, Development and implementing minimum two (2) projects in delivery of citizen services or schemes in the 7 (seven) years prior to the date of submission of bid.
rows.note: At least three cited are citizen-facing (statewide portal; land-records digitisation; municipal tax and permits).

rows.criterion: Sole Bidder must not be under a declaration of ineligibility / banned / blacklisted by any State or Central Government / any other Government institutions in India as on last date of submission of the Bid or convicted of economic offence in India as on last date of bid submission.
rows.note: Profile states not blacklisted/debarred and no conviction for an economic offence.

rows.criterion: Sole Bidder must have the following certifications: CMMI Level 5 (in development); ISO 9001; ISO 20000; ISO 27001; if any certificate is under renewal, last valid certificate plus self-declaration must be provided and the renewed certificate made available at least by opening of commercial bids, else disqualification; CMMI certificate should be verifiable on https://cmmiinstitute.com/pars.
rows.note: ISO 9001/20000/27001 are valid, but CMMI‑DEV Level 5 is lapsed and under renewal and the company is not listed on the CMMI PARS; to pass, a valid CMMI Level 5 (Development) certificate verifiable on PARS must be held by the required time.

rows.criterion: Sole Bidder must be registered with the Goods and Service Tax (GST) Authorities.
Board resolution/Power of attorney in favor of authorized signatory of Sole Bidder (in the name of the person executing the bid, authorizing the signatory to commit the Bidder).

rows.criterion: Sole Bidder must have at least 100 resources delivering IT / ITeS-related services on its payroll since 1st April 2022 to bid submission date, and must have at the time of bidding an office having at least 100 seats in India.

flags.title: Pre-bid conference date conflict
flags.detail: Two different dates are given for the pre-bid meeting/conference, creating uncertainty about when bidders can attend and when minutes will be issued.

evidence.quote: Pre-Bid meeting will be held on 13/08/2025 at 12:00 PM at the Board Room, Maharashtra Information Technology Corporation Limited, 3rd Floor, Apeejay House, Churchgate, Mumbai, Maharashtra – 400 020, for any suggestions or doubts regarding the RFP Document.

9. Date, Time and Venue of Pre-bid Conference 18/08/2025 and 12:00 Venue: Board Room, Maharashtra Information Technology Corporation Limited, 3rd Floor, Apeejay House, Churchgate, Mumbai, Maharashtra – 400 020

flags.recommendation: Raise a pre-bid query requesting a corrigendum clarifying the exact pre-bid conference date and time, and whether the 13/08/2025 event is only a query deadline or also a meeting.

flags.title: QCBS weighting vs normalization formula
flags.detail: The RFP states a 70% technical and 30% commercial QCBS weighting but then provides a technical normalization formula that scales to 15 points, which is inconsistent with a 70% weight for technical scores.

evidence.quote: This is a Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS). The technical evaluation marks would be given 70% weightage and commercial evaluation marks would be given 30% weightage to arrive at a composite score.
Formula that shall be used for normalization is: Normalized Score = (Score of Bidder / 100) * 15

flags.recommendation: Seek clarification on the correct technical normalization and composite score formula (e.g., confirm whether technical scores are to be scaled to 70, not 15) and request a corrected formula in a corrigendum.

flags.title: Unachievable API SLA and per‑call penalty
flags.detail: The API response time target of 0.30 milliseconds per call is not physically achievable for a web service, and the penalty is defined per API call, creating unlimited exposure.

evidence.quote: 3 API response time Time taken for system APIs to respond to external/internal service calls ≤ 0.30 ms per API call 1% of milestone payment per API call exceeding the response time in a given month

flags.recommendation: Request correction of the API target to a realistic figure (e.g., in milliseconds/seconds appropriate to network latency) and clarification that any penalty, if applicable, is aggregated and subject to an overall monthly cap.

flags.title: Conflicting uptime targets and penalty bases
flags.detail: Two different uptime baselines and penalty regimes are stated: 99.5% monthly with per‑0.1% penalties, and 98.5% quarterly with per‑0.5% penalties. This creates ambiguity on what is measured and enforced.

evidence.quote: 1 Aaple Sarkar 2.0 Portal Uptime Availability of the service delivery portal for end-users ≥ 99.5% uptime per calendar month 1% of milestone payment per 0.1% drop below threshold per month
3. SLA for Uptime For every 0.5 % drop in uptime in each quarter over the required uptime of 98.5% a penalty up to 0.25% of the Quarterly Invoice Value would be liable to be deducted.

flags.recommendation: Ask the Purchaser to confirm a single authoritative uptime metric (target, measurement period, and penalty formula) in a corrigendum and to withdraw the conflicting clause.

flags.title: Inconsistent GST treatment (inclusive vs extra)
flags.detail: The Fact Sheet says prices inclusive of all taxes including GST will be used for evaluation, while the Taxes clause says only GST will be paid by the Purchaser as part of payments, which implies GST is to be charged over the base price. This inconsistency affects price formation and evaluation parity.

evidence.quote: Prices inclusive of taxes (including GST) will be considered for arriving at the Composite Score.
19. Taxes Only Goods and Services Tax (GST) shall be paid by the Purchaser to the System Integrator as part of payments being made under the Contract that shall ensue in effect of this RFP Document.

flags.recommendation: Seek explicit instruction on whether bidders should quote prices inclusive or exclusive of GST and how evaluation will normalize bids; request alignment between evaluation and payment terms in a corrigendum.

flags.title: Undefined monthly SLA penalty cap referenced
flags.detail: The document refers to an overall SLA penalties cap per month but does not define the cap value or where it applies, leaving bidders exposed to uncertain aggregate penalties.

evidence.quote: These penalties will not be part of overall SLA penalties cap per month.

flags.recommendation: Request the definition and value of the overall monthly SLA penalty cap, its scope, and how it interacts with other penalties.

flags.title: Penalty cap inconsistency (100% of quarter vs 5% of O&M TCV)
flags.detail: One SLA imposes 100% of the Quarterly Payment as penalty for an 8‑hour outage, while another clause caps penalties to 5% of Total Contract Value for the O&M phase. Without clear precedence, these are irreconcilable.

evidence.quote: In case the services is not available for a continuous period of 8 Business Hours on any day, penaltyshall be 100% of the Quarterly Payment of the Project.
The maximum penalty will be up to five (5) % of Total Contract Value pertaining to the O&M phase.

flags.recommendation: Ask whether the 100% quarterly penalty is subject to the overall cap and to define a single penalty‑cap framework (monthly/quarterly and overall) applicable to all SLAs.

bullets: System Integrator to implement Maharashtra RTS Aaple Sarkar 2.0 for Government of Maharashtra, with a 9‑month implementation and 36 months of support (total 45 months).
Winner selected via QCBS with 70% technical and 30% financial weight (Bn = 0.70*Tn + 0.30*Fn); the document’s normalization formula conflicts with this and needs clarification.
Financial gates: Tender Fee INR 25,000; EMD INR 1,00,00,000 (Bank Guarantee); Performance Bank Guarantee ten (10) % of Total Contract Value; bid validity 180 days.
Submission is a four‑envelope process on https://www.mahatenders.gov.in; consortium not allowed; certifications required include CMMI Level 5 (Development) plus ISO 9001/20000/27001.

Material risk points include an unachievable API SLA (≤ 0.30 ms with per‑call penalties), conflicting uptime targets and penalty regimes, undefined or inconsistent penalty caps, and inconsistent GST treatment between evaluation and payments.
Key dates: pre‑bid queries close 13 August 2027 at 12:00, pre‑bid conference 18 August 2027 at 12:00, and bid submission closes 28 August 2027 at 17:00.
condensed: System Integrator for Maharashtra RTS Aaple Sarkar 2.0 (9‑month build + 36‑month support), selected via QCBS 70:30; fees and securities include INR 25,000 tender fee, INR 1,00,00,000 EMD, and PBG 10% of TCV.

Red flags: CMMI‑DEV L5 mandatory, four‑envelope submission, conflicting scoring and SLA/penalty clauses (0.30 ms API target, uptime and cap inconsistencies, GST evaluation vs payment); pre‑bid queries 13 Aug 2027 12:00; conference 18 Aug 2027 12:00; bid due 28 Aug 2027 17:00.
